newsitem.title: FRANCE: French multimedia firm IDP in IPO.
newsitem.headline: French multimedia firm IDP in IPO.

text.p: French multimedia company IDP said on Wednesday it was seeking a listing on the Paris Nouveau Marche start-up market with an Initial Public Offering for 23 to 29 percent of its capital.

In a statement IDP said it aimed to raise 30 million francs with the operation and would use the funds to finance its ambition to become a major player in the European and U.S. interactive audiovisual technologies.
IDP estimates sales for the fiscal year 1998/199 at 200 million francs. In the year to June 30, 1996, it had sales of 10.7 million francs.
Among IDP's financial partners are BNP funds Banexi Ventures and Finovectron and the Caisse des Depots.
IDP has been active for 10 years but it received a big boost in 1992 with the arrival of chairman Patrick Lafitte who became main shareholder in 1993.
It is now, it says, France's prime producer of multimedia products for third parties and counts L'Oreal, la Redoute, Hachette and Peugeot among its clients.
In 1996, the main shareholders of U.S. software group I2m -- Robert Thomson and Marco Arese Lucini -- swapped their company for a stake in IDP.
Among IDP's new products is StreamCAST which allows interactive television on a private network, such as in hotels, hospitals or cruise ships.
IDP gave no further details about the IPO.
